title: AuthPage
wrapsNative: ScrollView with scrollDismissesKeyboard(.interactively), a centred VStack limited with frame(maxWidth:), MonarchCard, and Link with MonarchLinkStyle
summary: A recipe, not a component: the centred, scrollable, keyboard-safe layout for sign-in, sign-up, password reset and verification screens, with the brand, a heading, an optional notice, the app's form, a footer line and small legal links.
whenToUse: For a screen that only asks people to sign in or create an account, before they reach the app.
whenNotToUse: When people sign in with Rook ID, use MonarchSignInWithRookButton on the welcome screen. For a password reset flow, see the password reset form recipe, which uses this layout.

states.name: plain
states.description: The form directly on the canvas: leave out the MonarchCard.

states.name: notice
states.description: A MonarchInlineNotice above the form, such as a session that expired.

states.name: keyboard up
states.description: The scroll view moves the focused field above the keyboard; dragging the content dismisses the keyboard.

appearance: The canvas background, the brand mark above, the title in the title style and the description in muted text, the form on the card surface, and caption-sized subtle links at the bottom.
platformNotes: The web AuthPage is a layout component with brand, notice, footer, links and a side panel above 1024 pixels. On iOS it is a recipe: the scroll view keeps the form clear of the keyboard, frame(maxWidth:) keeps it readable on iPad, and the side panel is left out (on iPad, put it in a NavigationSplitView sidebar if needed). Links open through openURL; the web's new-tab hint does not apply. The heading level becomes the header trait.
accessibility: The title has the header trait.
Fields come from MonarchTextField and MonarchPasswordInput, so labels and errors are read with them.
textContentType on the fields lets AutoFill offer the saved account and a strong password.
The legal links are links with 44-point touch targets from MonarchLinkStyle.
Everything scrolls at the largest text sizes; nothing is clipped by the keyboard.
edgeCases: Keep anything needed to sign in out of decorations: the brand mark is decorative.
On a device add keyboardType(.emailAddress) and textInputAutocapitalization(.never) to the email field; they are left out of the compiled example because the host build also targets macOS.
Set submitLabel and onSubmit so Return moves from email to password and then signs in.
